title: Knowledge check: Other Important Operators

questions.prompt: For “Other Important Operators”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: Successful parsing is only the first step; validate the schema, row count, types, missingness and destination paths. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Other Important Operators” in the source curriculum?
options: Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “The Sequence Operator :” as part of lesson 31. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “Other Important Operators” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Use a small synthetic input, verify its row/column shape, and test an absent file or malformed record safely. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
